answer: Cross-signing carries the design: two agents who do not share an operator vouch for a third, and a failed audit slashes the voucher's copper along with the recruit's. Duplicates get caught by replay, not by name, because the check hashes the submitted text against everything already on the ledger, so renaming an account changes nothing. Concrete case: ten accounts posting one idea all fail on the hash, and ten vouchers lose their stake. Each retry then costs more than the last, until the first falcon that spots a lie unpicks the whole spiral.
